name: Draft notice with missing party details
expected: Includes clean editable placeholders [Insert Landlord Address] without inventing a fake address.
prompt: Draft a legal notice to my landlord, but I don't know his full legal address.
raw_response:
### | Legal Notice

To,
[Landlord's Name or "Landlord"],
[Landlord's Address Line 1 - Placeholder: Enter known address or locality],
[City, State, Pincode].

**Subject: Legal notice for the refund of security deposit amounting to ₹[Insert Amount] in respect of premises located at [Insert Complete Property Address].**

Sir/Madam,

Under the instructions of and on behalf of my client, [Your Full Name], resident of [Your Current Address], I do hereby serve you with this legal notice under the applicable provisions of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 and the Model Tenancy Act, 2021, as follows:

1. That my client was a lawful tenant in respect of your residential/commercial premises situated at [Insert Complete Property Address] (hereinafter referred to as the "Demised Premises") under a tenancy agreement dated [Insert Date, if applicable] at a monthly rent of ₹[Insert Monthly Rent].

2. That my client faithfully paid all monthly rents on time and duly handed over vacant and peaceful possession of the Demised Premises to you on [Insert Date of Vacating] in the same condition as received, subject only to reasonable wear and tear, as contemplated under Section 108(m) of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882.

3. That at the commencement of the tenancy, my client paid an interest-free security deposit of ₹[Insert Security Deposit Amount], which is refundable upon the handover of vacant possession in accordance with Section 13 of the Model Tenancy Act, 2021.

4. That despite the peaceful surrender of the Demised Premises, you have illegally withheld the aforesaid security deposit of ₹[Insert Security Deposit Amount] without any valid justification or contractual basis, and have failed to communicate any lawful deductions.

I, therefore, through this notice, call upon you to refund the full security deposit of ₹[Insert Security Deposit Amount] to my client within 15 (fifteen) days from the receipt of this notice, failing which my client shall be constrained to initiate appropriate legal proceedings before the competent Rent Authority or Civil Court for recovery of the amount along with applicable interest and costs, at your sole risk and responsibility.

A copy of this notice is retained in my office for record and further necessary action.

Sincerely,

[Your Name]
(Through Counsel / Self)
[Your Phone Number]
[Your Email Address]

citations.title: Duration of certain leases in absence of written contract or local usage
citations.description: In the absence of a contract or local law to the contrary, a lease of immovable property for other than agricultural or manufacturing purposes is deemed to be month-to-month, terminable on 15 days' notice expiring with the end of a month of the tenancy.

citations.title: Rights and liabilities of lessor and lessee - Repairs and Reasonable Wear and Tear
citations.description: Lessee is bound to keep and restore the property in as good condition as it was at the time he was put in possession, subject only to reasonable wear and tear and irresistible force. Landlord cannot make arbitrary deductions for normal usage painting without explicit contractual basis.

citations.title: Cap on Security Deposit and Condition for Deductions
citations.description: Limits security deposit for residential premises to a maximum of two months' rent. Requires refund of security deposit to the tenant at the time of taking over vacant possession of the premises, after making valid deductions agreed under the tenancy agreement.
citations.jurisdiction: Model Central Act (Adopted by States such as AP, TN, UP)

citations.title: Suit by person dispossessed of immovable property without due process
citations.description: If any person is dispossessed without his consent of immovable property otherwise than in due course of law, he or any person claiming through him may, by suit, recover possession thereof notwithstanding any other title that may be set up.
